title: Increasing Enforcement against Cyclists and E-bike Users for Riding without Helmets, Front and Rear Lights, and Rising against Traffic Flow
what_it_is: Increasing Enforcement against Cyclists and E-bike Users for Riding without Helmets, Front and Rear Lights, and Rising against Traffic Flow

sections.label: On-road cycling offence enforcement
sections.summary: TP and LTA enforce against on-road cycling offences such as riding in groups over five, without helmets or lights, and against traffic flow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: TP and LTA enforce against on-road cycling offences, including riding in groups of more than five, without helmets, without front and rear lights, and going against the flow of traffic.

sections.label: Stricter sentences for motorists
sections.summary: The Member asks authorities to consider that harsher punishment for a motorist may not always be fair if the cyclist was blatantly non-compliant with the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: With the recent practices of the prosecution and the Courts asking or imposing stricter sentences, including custodial sentences when a person is injured in a traffic accident, I would like to ask the authorities to consider that it would not always be as fair for a motorist to receive harsher punishment if he is involved in an accident with a cyclist who is blatantly not compliant with the law, for example, riding against traffic, beating red lights, not having lights at night or even not wearing helmets and risking more serious injury during an accident.

sections.label: Holistic culpability assessment in traffic cases
sections.summary: TP assesses culpability holistically when preferring charges, so no road user type is blamed disproportionately, and cyclists and e-bike users are treated like motorised vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As for culpability, when TP investigates cases and when assessing what kind of charges should be preferred against those who violate traffic rules, culpability will be assessed holistically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: And so, I wish to assure the Member that the circumstances will be looked into, and it would not be the case where there will always be one type of road users who are blamed disproportionately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The entire situation of how the accident was caused must be looked into and I believe that is also the approach that our Courts take.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: And as for repeat offenders, cyclists and e-bike users are treated like our cars and other kinds of motorised vehicles on the roads in the sense that we expect them to keep to our traffic rules, we expect them to observe them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The kinds of enforcement that we take are also similar.
